messages: Clara - Design: quick design sync question about the 'panic' action for rollouts. current mock puts a red "panic" floating action in the bottom-right over the timeline. On mobile it's close to the scrubber and the floating keyboard on iOS hides it. screenshot: https://img.redwood.dev/mock/panic-button-overlap.png Diego - Eng: yep that's problematic. Two immediate options: 1) pin panic to the top-right global header (always visible) 2) keep it contextual near the timeline but anchor to the timeline header (right side) so it doesn't overlap scrubber. Both have pros/cons. Rowan - PM: product perspective: we want panic to be discoverable quickly but also resilient to accidental taps. Top-right global makes it discoverable but divorced from the rollout context. Contextual near timeline keeps locality but could be occluded. Preference? Clara - Design: leaning toward contextual but with extra safety: make it a two-step control. First tap morphs into a larger confirmation surface attached to the timeline: "Panic rollback 3 Confirm" with short explanation. This keeps users sure of intent. Diego - Eng: engineering constraints: can't change DOM order for SR; if we absolutely position the confirmation surface we must ensure it's reachable by keyboard and announced. Also mobile safe-area inset (iPhone notch) can push touch target; we should respect env(safe-area-inset-*). a11y-bot: accessibility checklist: confirmation must be keyboard focusable, aria-modal for destructive confirm, aria-describedby pointing to reason text, assertive announcement for rollbacks, color contrast >=4.5:1 for small text, and focus trap when modal is open. Don't move keyboard focus automatically unless necessary; provide a skip link pattern. Rowan - PM: copy options for primary label: (A) "Panic rollback" (B) "Emergency rollback" (C) "Stop & rollback". We need to avoid alarming language but be explicit. Which reads best for users and auditors? Clara - Design: prefer C "Stop & rollback" 3 less dramatic but clear. Secondary small text: "Routes traffic to stable and reverts to last safe version". CTA flow: primary "Confirm rollback" secondary "Cancel". Add a tertiary "Open inspector" for context. Diego - Eng: interaction idea: first interaction is an inline expansion (not modal) with keyboard-accessible Confirm. For high-trust orgs (Dedicated/Private) where we have stricter policies, the Confirm should open a modal with required justification field and optional approval workflow. We can toggle by org config. a11y-bot: announce pattern: when expanding inline: update aria-live region with "Stop & rollback expanded. Confirm to proceed." For modal: set role="dialog" aria-labelledby to title and move focus into first input. Ensure Escape closes and returns focus to the panic button. Clara - Design: visual notes: red for the panic surface should be a desaturated red (not full #FF0000) to avoid visual shock; ensure the button label contrast meets AA. Add shield+arrow icon to indicate rollback action. For floating placement use a 16px margin from right and bottom and respect env(safe-area-inset-bottom). Rowan - PM: telemetry we need: panic_shown, panic_expand_clicked, panic_confirmed, panic_cancelled, panic_justification_submitted, panic_failed. Also measure time-to-confirm and accidental_cancel_rate. Diego - Eng: keyboard order: when inline expansion appears we should NOT steal focus. Instead add a visible skip link right after the panic button: "Go to confirm" shown on :focus. That avoids trapping users. For modal flows we'll move focus into the dialog. a11y-bot: reduced-motion: any expansion should animate with reduced-motion respect and complete within 160ms. For screenreader users prefer no animation. Clara - Design: mobile alt-flow: if width <360px collapse into a full-width bar pinned to top of timeline (not bottom) to avoid keyboard overlap. Add a small handle so users can still access scrubber easily. Rowan - PM: one more governance detail: only users with rollback permission should see the panic control. For others show a greyed-out 'Assistance' action which opens a help flow. Track permission-based impressions. Diego - Eng: implementation note: we'll gate by feature flag and include AR checks: `if (!user.canRollback) { renderAssistance(); }` Also namespace classes to avoid private console CSS bleed: `.rw-panic-control` with explicit z-index layering. Clara - Design: final action items: 1) I'll update comps with contextual right-anchored panic that expands inline + full-width mobile alt + desat red swatch. 2) Diego to prototype skip-link pattern and modal justification form for dedicated orgs. 3) Rowan to add telemetry + permission gating to ticket. 4) a11y-bot to add test checklist. Will upload frames by EOD and tag everyone. Rowan - PM: thanks all 3 prioritizing for next sprint. tagging @diego @a11y-bot. :rocket:
